{{URL|urbanoutfitters.com|Commercial website}} * {{URL|urbn.com|Corporate website}} }} }} '''Urban Outfitters, Inc.''' is a multinational [[Lifestyle brand|lifestyle]] retail corporation headquartered in [[Philadelphia]], Pennsylvania.{{Cite web|date=April 12, 2019|title=Asian Urban Outfitters Exec: Millennial Staffers Called Me "Mr. Miyagi"|url=https://www.phillymag.com/news/2019/04/12/urban-outfitters-lawsuit/|access-date=June 29, 2020|website=Philadelphia Magazine|language=en-US}} Operating in the United States, the United Kingdom, Canada, select Western European countries, Poland,{{Cite web|last=Hughes|first=Huw|date=May 31, 2019|title=Urban Outfitters picks Warsaw for first Central European store|url=https://fashionunited.uk/news/retail/urban-outfitters-chooses-warsaw-for-first-central-european-store/2019053143454|access-date=June 29, 2020|website=fashionunited.uk|language=en-gb}} the United Arab Emirates, and Qatar, the Urban Outfitters brand targets young adults with a merchandise mix of women's and men's fashion apparel, footwear, beauty and wellness products, accessories, [[activewear]] and gear, and [[housewares]], as well as music, primarily [[vinyl records]] and [[Cassette tape|cassettes]]. The company was founded as the retail store [[Free People]] by [[Richard Hayne]], Judy Wicks and Scott Belair in 1970 as a project for an entrepreneurship class at [[University of Pennsylvania]].{{Cite web|url=http://www.urbn.com/who-we-are/history|title=History|website=URBN|language=en|access-date=April 3, 2018}} It was renamed to Urban Outfitters and incorporated in 1976. Urban Outfitters carries multiple stores within its portfolio of brands, which also includes Urban Outfitters itself, [[Anthropologie]], [[Free People]], Terrain, [[BHLDN]] and the Vetri Family restaurant group. Much of the merchandise is designed and produced by the company's wholesale division on these multiple private labels.{{Cite web|title=urbn-10k_20190131.htm|url=https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/912615/000156459019010433/urbn-10k_20190131.htm|access-date=June 29, 2020|website=www.sec.gov}} ==History== In the 1970s, Scott Belair & Dick Hayne opened a store and called it Free People in [[West Philadelphia]], Pennsylvania. As the store eventually grew from one to two storefronts, the name was changed from Free People to Urban Outfitters.{{cite web|url=https://www.freepeople.com/help/our-story/|website=Free People|title=Our Story|access-date=October 28, 2021|archive-date=October 28, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211028192720/https://www.freepeople.com/help/our-story/|url-status=dead}} [[File: Urban Outfitters Barrington Street Halifax.jpg|thumb|left|Urban Outfitters store in [[Halifax, Nova Scotia]]]] In 2007, the company received the National Preservation Honor Award from the [[National Trust for Historic Preservation]] for the Urban Outfitters Corporate Office Campus located on the [[Philadelphia Naval Shipyard]].{{Why|date=December 2022}}{{cite web| title = NTHP Presents Honor Award To Urban Outfitters Corporate Office Campus| publisher = National Trust| url = http://press.nationaltrust.org/index.php?option=com_content&task=view&id=183&Itemid=162| access-date = February 18, 2009| archive-date = November 23, 2007| archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20071123050055/http://press.nationaltrust.org/index.php?option=com_content&task=view&id=183&Itemid=162| url-status = dead}} In 2011, it agreed to sell limited editions of [[List of Polaroid instant cameras#600|Polaroid ONE600]] [[instant camera]]s and Type 779 [[instant film]] in partnership with the Austrian entrepreneur Florian Kaps, who acquired the rights to manufacture 700 copies of the defunct product.Karen von Hahn, "Mama, don't take my Polaroid away", ''Globe and Mail'', page L3, September 5, 2009 In January 2013, it hired the Abraham & Roetzel lobbying firm, led by former Republican Sen. [[Spencer Abraham]], to advocate on its behalf in [[Washington, D.C.]], regarding retail industry policy.{{cite web|url=http://www.publicintegrity.org/2013/01/29/12095/influence-chic-urban-outfitters-bags-k-street-help|website=[[Center for Public Integrity]]|title=Influence chic: Urban Outfitters bags K Street help|date=29 January 2013|last=Levinthal|first=Dave}} In Q4 2015, the company announced plans to acquire the Vetri Family, a Philadelphia restaurant group. As the company was facing declining same store sales and foot traffic, the acquisition illustrated the retailer's shift in strategy. This includes restaurants Amis Trattoria, Bar Amis, and Pizzeria Vetri. There are two Pizzeria Vetri locations in Philadelphia, with other locations in [[King of Prussia, Pennsylvania]], [[Devon, Pennsylvania]] and Washington, D.C.{{Cite news | title=This Is the Reason Urban Outfitters Bought a Pizza Chain | url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2016-07-20/why-urban-outfitters-bought-philadelphia-s-pizzeria-vetri | first=Peter | last=Elliot | work=[[Bloomberg News]] | date=July 20, 2016 |url-access=subscription }} In 2019, the company drew attention by announcing the sale of used [[VHS tapes]] for $40.{{Cite web|url=http://www.purplerevolver.com/movies/movie-news/127625-urban-outfitters-launch-random%2C-used-vhs-sets-for-%2440.html|title=Urban Outfitters launch random, used VHS sets for $40 > Movie News > Movies | Purple Revolver|date=20 February 2019|access-date=18 December 2022|website=purplerevolver.com|last=Deen|first=Khyle }} In the same year, Urban Outfitters launched Nuuly, a subscription clothing rental service. Following that, the company launched Nuuly Thrift, a resale platform for buying and selling women's, men's and kids’ apparel and accessories from URBN labels and other brands.{{Cite news |last=Edelson |first=Sharon |date=24 August 2021 |title=After A Successful 2019 Rental Service Launch, Urban Outfitters Is Diving Into Resale With Nuuly |work=Forbes |url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/sharonedelson/2021/08/24/after-a-successful-rental-service-launch-in-2019-nuuly-is-diving-into-resale/?sh=1337ad5940f5}} As of 2020, Urban Outfitters does not publicly disclose which factories produce the brand's clothing.{{cite news |last1=Kashyap |first1=Aruna |title=When Clothing Labels Are a Matter of Life or Death |url=https://www.thedailybeast.com/when-clothing-labels-are-a-matter-of-life-or-death |website=The Daily Beast |date=May 2, 2018 |publisher=The Daily Beast |access-date=April 16, 2020}} It also has no human resources department. In December 2022, Urban Outfitters announced the departure of its president, Francis Pierrel, from the company.{{Cite web |date=2 Dec 2022 |title=Personnel Changes |url=https://www.nasdaq.com/press-release/urbn-announces-personnel-changes-2022-12-02 |website=Nasdaq}}{{Cite web |last=Ell |first=Kellie |date=2022-12-02 |title=Urban Outfitters Brand President Francis Pierrel Exits |url=https://wwd.com/business-news/human-resources/urban-outfitters-brand-president-francis-pierrel-leaves-1235435899/ |access-date=2022-12-05 |website=WWD |language=en-US}} == Criticism == Urban Outfitters' products have also been the subject of multiple complaints and criticism, largely from religious, ethical, and ethnic pressure groups including a local chapter of the [[NAACP]],[http://www.sptimes.com/2003/10/04/Tampabay/Game_s_street_theme_u.shtml "Game's street theme upsets NAACP"] — ''St. Petersburg Times''{{cite news| title = Black leaders outraged at 'Ghettopoly' game at Urban Outfitters | work = USA Today | url = https://www.usatoday.com/news/nation/2003-10-09-ghettopoly_x.htm| date=October 9, 2003 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20040701165949/https://www.usatoday.com/news/nation/2003-10-09-ghettopoly_x.htm |archive-date=July 1, 2004 | access-date=May 27, 2010}} [[Anti-Defamation League]]{{cite web |title=Urban Outfitters Discontinues Offensive T-Shirt |url=https://www.adl.org/PresRele/DiRaB_41/4438_41.htm |website=ADL |access-date=July 24, 2021 |date=January 9, 2004|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20041114092914/https://www.adl.org/PresRele/DiRaB_41/4438_41.htm |archive-date=November 14, 2004 |url-status=dead}} and [[Navajo Nation]] for some of their products. In January 2007, Urban Outfitters stopped selling [[Keffiyeh|keffiyehs]] after Jewish blogging site ''Jewschool'' called out the company for describing the item as an "anti-war woven scarf".{{Cite web |last=Kim |first=Kibum |date=11 February 2007 |title=Where Some See Fashion, Others See Politics |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2007/02/11/fashion/shows/11KAFFIYEH.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210512084350/https://www.nytimes.com/2007/02/11/fashion/shows/11KAFFIYEH.html |archive-date=12 May 2021 |website=The New York Times}} ===Labor practices=== On November 27, 2009, Urban Outfitters drew the attention of the Swedish press for denying collective bargaining rights to employees at their [[Stockholm]] store by making all 38 workers [[Layoff|redundant]] and re-hiring them through [[employment agency]] Academic Work.{{cite web| title = Sparkas efter krav på kollektivavtal| work = Aftonbladet |author=Catarina Håkansson |date=November 27, 2009| url = http://www.aftonbladet.se/nyheter/article6196828.ab}}{{cite web| title = Sparkas efter krav på kollektivavtal| website = Dagenshandel.se |author=Jesper Stärn |date=November 27, 2009| url = http://www.dagenshandel.se/dh/DagensH.nsf/0/2B94C91443B64263C125767B0029F360?open| access-date = November 27, 2009| archive-date = November 29, 2009| archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20091129002959/http://www.dagenshandel.se/dh/DagensH.nsf/0/2B94C91443B64263C125767B0029F360?open| url-status = dead}} In response to the move, [[ombudsman]] Jimmy Ekman called for tougher laws to prevent other firms denying [[collective bargaining]] rights in this way.{{cite news| title = Antingen skriver man på eller blir uppsagd| newspaper = Svenska Dagbladet| date = November 27, 2009| publisher = Svenska Dagbladet, By [[Negra Efendić]], November 27, 2010| url = http://www.svd.se/naringsliv/nyheter/artikel_3857527.svd| last1 = Efendić| first1 = Negra}} In 2019, a former executive of Chinese descent with 40 years at the company sued it for ethnic and [[age-based discrimination]]. In 2021, the company only received a score of 11–20% in the Fashion Transparency Index. There is also no evidence of Urban Outfitters ensuring the paying of living wages to their employees.{{cite web |url=https://goodonyou.eco/how-ethical-is-urban-outfitters/|title=How Ethical Is Urban Outfitters? |date=September 6, 2022 }} ==References== {{reflist}} ==External links== * [http://urbanoutfitters.com Commercial website] * [https://urbn.com Corporate website]{{Finance links | name = Urban Outfitters | symbol = URBN | sec_cik = URBN | yahoo = URBN | google = URBN }} {{Urban Outfitters |state=expanded}} {{Philadelphia Corporations}} {{Portal bar|Philadelphia|Companies}} {{Authority control}} [[Category:1970 establishments in Pennsylvania]] [[Category:Clothing brands of the United States]] [[Category:Clothing retailers of the United States]] [[Category:Companies based in Philadelphia]] [[Category:Companies listed on the Nasdaq]] [[Category:Cultural appropriation]] [[Category:Retail companies established in 1970]]

Urban Outfitters, Inc. is a multinational lifestyle retail corporation headquartered in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. Operating in the United States, the United Kingdom, Canada, select Western European countries, Poland, the United Arab Emirates, and Qatar, the Urban Outfitters brand targets young adults with a merchandise mix of women's and men's fashion apparel, footwear, beauty and wellness products, accessories, activewear and gear, and housewares, as well as music, primarily vinyl records and cassettes.
The company was founded as the retail store Free People by Richard Hayne, Judy Wicks and Scott Belair in 1970 as a project for an entrepreneurship class at University of Pennsylvania. It was renamed to Urban Outfitters and incorporated in 1976.
Urban Outfitters carries multiple stores within its portfolio of brands, which also includes Urban Outfitters itself, Anthropologie, Free People, Terrain, BHLDN and the Vetri Family restaurant group. Much of the merchandise is designed and produced by the company's wholesale division on these multiple private labels.
